rows.description: End-to-end encrypted notes, tasks, files, passwords, journal and bookmarks. Keyed by a 12-word BIP-39 phrase: no email, no password, no account to leak. The full client source for web, desktop and mobile is published, along with the encryption (XChaCha20-Poly1305, HKDF-SHA256, Ed25519) and the threat model, so the privacy claims are falsifiable.
headings: ### What your data looks like on our server
## The parts that are not absolute
### Custodial mode, the exception to the first claim
feature_signals: **Notes, tasks, and journal, encrypted on your device.**
| Your notes are encrypted on your device, at rest and on the way to us | [`crypto/crypto.ts`](crypto/crypto.ts), the XChaCha20-Poly1305 path |

**Note encryption.** Each note is encrypted with XChaCha20-Poly1305 under a random 24-byte nonce. The plaintext payload includes title, body, tags, and metadata such as trashed and starred state. The server sees none of it. The 24-byte nonce is what makes random generation safe without collision risk, unlike AES-GCM's 12 bytes.
import { generateMnemonic, mnemonicToSeedSync } from '@scure/bip39';
const seed   = mnemonicToSeedSync(phrase);
console.log('Deterministic    :', hex(hkdf(sha256, mnemonicToSeedSync(phrase), undefined, utf8.encode('privacynotes-encryption-v1'), 32)) === hex(encKey));
- **Metadata.** The server sees your public key, ciphertext sizes, timestamps, note counts, request IPs and sync patterns.
- **OAuth.** A Google, Apple or GitHub sign-in links that provider's email to your key, custodial or not.
- **Web code.** A browser fetches the app's code again on every visit, so if your threat model includes us being coerced, prefer the signed native apps.
- **Your device.** Malware on your device reads what you read, and a lost phrase under self-custody means lost notes.

rows.description: A simple text field for adding quick notes without ads.
Offline-first Android planner with calendar, tasks, bills, scanning and natural-language Quick entry
feature_signals: Enjoying Planner? Buy me a coffee to help support its development. Thank you!
- Offline natural-language Quick entry with editable previews.

- Turn a task into an event or an event into a task, Undo/Redo while typing in the editors, and templates for one event or a set of events (a weekend away, added again from any day). Repeating tasks show their streak ("🔥 5 in a row"), and a Habits page shows how often each was done on time.

- Calendars beside your own: Nextcloud, the calendars on your phone, your contacts' birthdays (with optional reminders and Message and Call buttons) and calendar links, shown read-only; one Nextcloud calendar can be kept in sync both ways, automatically while Planner is open.
- Notes in Markdown with checklists, notebooks, tags, colours, attachments and reminders; optional two-way sync with the Nextcloud Notes app (and so with Quillpad).
- Document and bill scanning with cropping and on-device text recognition.
- Matrix Green, High Contrast and Colour-blind friendly themes.
- Two home-screen widgets: today, and the next seven days.
- Checks GitHub for new versions once a day (optional) and asks before downloading or installing.
- Report a bug from the ⋮ menu: it opens a prefilled GitHub issue and shows exactly what will be sent.
1. Clone this repository and open its root folder in Android Studio.
2. Install Android SDK platform 35 and let Gradle sync using the checked-in versions.
3. Use JDK 21 for Gradle. The daemon configuration requests JetBrains JDK 21 and can download it when needed.
4. Run the `app` configuration on an emulator or phone running Android 8.0 (API 26) or later.
